milestones.title: Septuagint (LXX)
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Jewish scholars in Alexandria, Egypt
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first translation of the Hebrew Scriptures, begun with the Torah for Greek-speaking Jews. It became the Bible of the early church and is quoted throughout the New Testament.

milestones.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls are copied
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Scribes of a Jewish community near Qumran and elsewhere
milestones.historicalSignificance: Copies of every Old Testament book except Esther (and Nehemiah, unless counted with Ezra), hidden in caves before the Roman destruction of Qumran.

milestones.title: Old Latin (Vetus Latina)
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Unknown translators in North Africa and Italy
milestones.historicalSignificance: Early, uneven Latin versions used by Tertullian and Cyprian, later revised by Jerome.

milestones.title: Syriac Peshitta
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Syriac-speaking churches around Edessa
milestones.historicalSignificance: The 'simple' version: the Old Testament translated from Hebrew, the New Testament standardised by the early 5th century. Still the Bible of Syriac churches today.

milestones.title: Papyrus 52 (John 18)
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Egypt; now in the John Rylands Library, Manchester
milestones.historicalSignificance: A scrap of John 18:31–33, 37–38 — often cited as the earliest known New Testament fragment, copied within decades of the Gospel’s writing.

milestones.title: Coptic versions
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Egyptian churches (Sahidic, then Bohairic dialects)
milestones.historicalSignificance: Brought Scripture to Egyptian-speaking Christians and monks; the Bohairic version remains the liturgical text of the Coptic Church.

milestones.title: Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Greek scribes, probably in Egypt or Caesarea
milestones.historicalSignificance: The oldest near-complete Bibles, copied in the generation of the Council of Nicaea. Sinaiticus contains the oldest complete New Testament.

milestones.title: Gothic Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Bishop Wulfila (Ulfilas)
milestones.historicalSignificance: Wulfila invented a Gothic alphabet to translate the Bible — the earliest substantial text in any Germanic language.

milestones.title: Latin Vulgate
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Jerome, commissioned by Pope Damasus I
milestones.historicalSignificance: Jerome returned to the Hebrew for the Old Testament. The 'common' (vulgata) Bible of the West for a thousand years; declared authentic at the Council of Trent (1546).

milestones.title: Armenian Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Mesrop Mashtots and Patriarch Sahak
milestones.historicalSignificance: Mesrop created the Armenian alphabet so the Bible could be translated; the version is called 'the queen of translations'.

milestones.title: Old Church Slavonic
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Cyril and Methodius, missionaries to Moravia
milestones.historicalSignificance: The brothers devised the Glagolitic alphabet; their work shaped the Cyrillic script and the worship of the Slavic churches.

milestones.title: Wycliffe Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: John Wycliffe and associates (Nicholas of Hereford, John Purvey)
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first complete Bible in English, copied by hand from the Vulgate. Unlicensed English translation was banned in 1409, yet some 250 manuscripts survive.

milestones.title: Gutenberg Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Johannes Gutenberg, Mainz
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first major book printed with movable metal type in Europe, opening the way for cheap, standardised Bibles.

milestones.title: Erasmus’s Greek New Testament
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Desiderius Erasmus, printed by Froben in Basel
milestones.targetLanguage: Greek with a new Latin translation
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first published Greek New Testament. Its later editions underlie the Textus Receptus used by Luther, Tyndale and the King James translators.

milestones.title: Luther Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Martin Luther, Wartburg Castle and Wittenberg
milestones.historicalSignificance: The 'September Testament' was translated in about eleven weeks. It shaped modern standard German and spread through the new printing presses.

milestones.title: Tyndale New Testament
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: William Tyndale, printed at Worms
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first printed English New Testament and the first translated from Greek. Tyndale was executed in 1536, but much of his wording survives in the King James Version.

milestones.title: Coverdale Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Myles Coverdale
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first complete printed Bible in English; its Psalms lived on in the Book of Common Prayer.

milestones.title: Geneva Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: English Protestant exiles in Geneva (William Whittingham and others)
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first English Bible with both chapters and numbered verses, in readable roman type with study notes — the Bible of Shakespeare and the Pilgrims.

milestones.title: Reina–Valera (Biblia del Oso)
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Casiodoro de Reina; revised by Cipriano de Valera
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first complete Bible in Spanish from the original languages; its revisions remain the most widely read Spanish Protestant Bible.

milestones.title: King James Version
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: 47 scholars in six companies at Westminster, Oxford and Cambridge
milestones.historicalSignificance: Authorised by James I; the most influential English Bible for three centuries and a foundation of English literature.

milestones.title: Eliot Indian Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: John Eliot with Algonquian translators
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first complete Bible printed in the Americas — in an Indigenous language.

milestones.title: Bengali New Testament
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: William Carey and the Serampore Mission, India
milestones.historicalSignificance: The start of the modern missionary translation movement; Serampore produced Scripture in some 40 languages and dialects.

milestones.title: British and Foreign Bible Society founded
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: London
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first of the Bible societies that funded translation and printing worldwide, later joined by the American Bible Society (1816).

milestones.title: Chinese Bible
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Robert Morrison and William Milne
milestones.historicalSignificance: The first complete Protestant Bible in Chinese, printed at Malacca.

milestones.title: Codex Sinaiticus discovered
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Constantin von Tischendorf at St Catherine’s Monastery, Sinai
milestones.historicalSignificance: Brought a 4th-century complete New Testament to scholarly attention, transforming textual criticism.

milestones.title: SIL and Wycliffe Bible Translators
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: William Cameron Townsend
milestones.historicalSignificance: Linguistic training (1934) and a translation mission (1942) focused on languages that had no written Scripture.

milestones.title: Dead Sea Scrolls discovered
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Qumran caves, near the Dead Sea
milestones.historicalSignificance: The Great Isaiah Scroll (c. 125 BC) is about a thousand years older than the previous oldest complete Hebrew manuscripts of Isaiah, yet agrees closely with the medieval Masoretic text apart from spelling and minor variants — strong evidence of careful transmission.

milestones.title: Global Scripture access today
milestones.translatorOrOrigin: Wycliffe Global Alliance / ProgressBible
milestones.historicalSignificance: Translation work is in progress in 4,457 languages; 544 languages (36.8 million people) are still waiting for it to begin. More than 99% of people have at least some Scripture in a language they understand.
